content.title: Helping technical teams move together
content.intro: A technical project coordinator helps people understand what is happening, what comes next, and what could slow the work down.

sections.title: Coordination creates clarity
body: Developers, designers, marketers, and stakeholders often depend on one another. A coordinator keeps the shared goal, current tasks, owners, and deadlines
so nobody has to guess what is happening.

sections.title: The role removes obstacles
sections.body: A coordinator does not need to write the code. They notice missing decisions, unclear ownership, and blocked work, then help the right people resolve them.

next.title: Check the coordinator mindset
next.body: Use this idea to choose the clearest response to two everyday team situations.

content.title: Check technical team coordination
content.intro: Choose the response that makes work clearer and easier to move forward.

questions.prompt: A developer cannot start because a design has not been approved. What should the coordinator do first?
options: Make the dependency visible and ask the design owner for a decision
Tell the developer to build something else without updating the plan
Wait until the next weekly meeting
questions.explanation: The coordinator makes the blocked dependency visible and brings the right owner into the decision.

questions.prompt: Which project update is most useful to a team?
options: Invite testing is blocked until Sam approves the design by Thursday
questions.explanation: A useful update names the work, its current state, the dependency, the owner, and the needed timing.

completion.title: You understand the coordinator’s role!
completion.body: You learned how coordinators create clarity, expose dependencies, and help technical teams keep moving.
